name: kiro-acp
description: Chat with the Kiro agent inside VS Code over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). Spawns `kiro-cli acp` locally; the extension itself makes no network calls.

commands.title: Kiro: Send Selection to Kiro Chat
Kiro: Open Past Session in Sidebar…

kiroAcp.cliPath.description: Path to the kiro-cli executable. A bare name is resolved on PATH, then in the default install locations for the platform.

kiroAcp.cliArgs.description: Extra arguments appended after `acp`, for example ["--agent-engine=v3"].

kiroAcp.agentProcesses.max.markdownDescription: How many `kiro-cli acp` processes may run at once. Each session gets a process of its own, so sessions in different chat tabs work in parallel (one process runs one turn at a time); every process costs memory. Past the limit, new sessions share the least busy process and take turns there. `1` runs every session in one shared process, as before. Applies at the next start or `Kiro: Restart Agent Process`.

kiroAcp.fs.allowedWriteRoots.markdownDescription: Folders outside the workspace that Kiro may write files to without asking (writes elsewhere outside the workspace show a confirmation, whose **Always allow** button adds the file's folder here). `${tmpdir}` is the system temp folder; `~`, `${home}` and `${env:NAME}` are expanded; an entry that does not resolve to an absolute path is ignored. User settings only: a workspace cannot widen it.

kiroAcp.attachActiveFile.description: Attach the active editor file to each prompt as a resource link (shown as a removable chip). Off by default: add files explicitly with @ or the Send Selection command.

enumDescriptions: Open a diff editor for every file change the agent proposes, even when it is applied without asking.
Open a diff editor only when a file change waits for your permission (default).
Never open diff editors automatically; use the links in the chat.
kiroAcp.autoOpenDiffs.description: When to open the native diff editor for file changes proposed by the agent. In autonomous modes tool calls complete without a permission request; opening a tab for each would hide the chat.

enumDescriptions: One VS Code terminal per Kiro session (default): every agent command writes its header, output and exit code into it. It is revealed once, on the session's first command.
One VS Code terminal per agent command, revealed when the command starts.
No VS Code terminal; command output is only shown in the chat card.
kiroAcp.terminal.mode.description: How terminals opened by the agent are shown. Read when each command starts, so a change applies to the next command.

kiroAcp.terminal.outputByteLimit.description: Default byte limit retained for agent-requested terminal output when the agent does not specify one.

kiroAcp.logProtocol.description: Write every JSON-RPC message to the 'Kiro ACP' output channel (useful when reporting bugs).

enumDescriptions: Open the chat as a tab in the editor area (default).
Open the chat in the Kiro view of the secondary side bar.
kiroAcp.chatLocation.description: Where `Kiro: Focus Chat`, permission requests and `Send Selection` open the chat.

kiroAcp.showSettingsByDefault.description: Show the mode / model / option pickers without pressing the settings button in the chat.

kiroAcp.sessionPanelCollapsed.description: Start the chat with the session list collapsed to icons.

kiroAcp.rememberSessionOptions.description: Remember the mode, model and config options you choose and apply them to every new session (only values the agent advertises are applied). `Kiro: Forget Remembered Session Options` clears them.

kiroAcp.agentLink.enabled.markdownDescription: Experimental. Give every Kiro session a small MCP server (`kiro-acp-tabs`) on `127.0.0.1` so the agents in different chat tabs can work together: list and read the other sessions, send them messages, wait for them and start new ones (see `kiroAcp.agentLink.confirm` and `kiroAcp.agentLink.maxChain`). Each session gets its own token; nothing outside this machine can reach it. Applies to sessions created after the change; turning it off cuts the live sessions off too.

kiroAcp.agentLink.maxChain.markdownDescription: Agent link: how many turns in a row agents may start in each other's sessions (`send_message`, `start_session`) before the next message is refused and both chats say the chain was stopped. A message you type yourself starts the count over. Guards against two agents answering each other for ever.

kiroAcp.agentLink.autoApprove.markdownDescription: Answer Kiro's own permission requests for the agent-link tools (`kiro-acp-tabs`: list, read, send, wait, start) automatically, so a conversation between sessions does not show Kiro's card for every message. Sending and starting are still guarded by `#kiroAcp.agentLink.confirm#`; set that to `never` as well to be asked nothing at all. Other tools and other MCP servers are not affected.

enumDescriptions: Ask in the sending chat before a session first messages another one; once you allow it, that session may message the other until either closes (default). Starting a new session always asks.
Ask before every message and every new session.
Never ask: agents message each other and start sessions on their own (the chain and rate limits still apply).
kiroAcp.agentLink.confirm.markdownDescription: Agent link: when to ask you before an agent sends a message to another session (`send_message`) or starts a new one (`start_session`). The question is a card in the sending chat with **Send** / **Don't send**.

scripts.test: npm run typecheck && npm run compile-tests && node --test "out/test/**/*.test.js"
scripts.test:e2e: npm run build && npm run compile-e2e && node scripts/run-e2e.mjs
scripts.package: npm run typecheck && npm run build && vsce package --no-dependencies
